passages.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lilies of the Covenant.” A Psalm of Asaph.
passages.sermon: This psalm is for the choirmaster.\r\nThe psalm uses the tune called “The Lilies of the Covenant.”\r\nAsaph wrote this psalm.

passages.text: Hear us, O Shepherd of Israel, who leads Joseph like a flock; You who sit enthroned between the cherubim, shine forth before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Rally Your mighty power and come to save us.
passages.sermon:
This is a psalm of Asaph.
The psalm is for the choirmaster.
It is to be sung to the tune “The Lilies of the Covenant.”
God is the Shepherd of Israel.
God leads Joseph like a flock of sheep.
God sits enthroned between the cherubim.
God, listen to us.
God, show Yourself.
Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh are before You.
God, awaken Your strength.
God, come and save us.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ אֶל־ שֹׁשַׁנִּ֑ים עֵד֖וּת לְאָסָ֣ף מִזְמֽוֹר׃ רֹ֘עֵ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל׀ הַאֲזִ֗ינָה נֹהֵ֣ג כַּצֹּ֣אן יוֹסֵ֑ף יֹשֵׁ֖ב הַכְּרוּבִ֣ים הוֹפִֽיעָה׃ לִפְנֵ֤י אֶפְרַ֨יִם׀ וּבִנְיָ֘מִ֤ן וּמְנַשֶּׁ֗ה עוֹרְרָ֥ה אֶת־ גְּבֽוּרָתֶ֑ךָ וּלְכָ֖ה לִישֻׁעָ֣תָה לָּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
passages.sermon: God, restore us.\r\nShine Your face on us.\r\nSave us.

passages.text: O LORD God of Hosts, how long will Your anger smolder against the prayers of Your people?
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God of Hosts.
He rules over all heavenly armies.
He is powerful and mighty.
The people belong to Him.
They pray to Him.
His anger burns against their prayers.
His anger does not end quickly.
The people ask, “How long will You stay angry?”
They want God to stop being angry with their prayers.
passages.original: יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְבָא֑וֹת עַד־ מָתַ֥י עָ֝שַׁ֗נְתָּ בִּתְפִלַּ֥ת עַמֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: You fed them with the bread of tears and made them drink the full measure of their tears.
passages.sermon:
God gave His people food.
This food was the bread of tears.
God made His people drink.
They drank a full measure of their own tears.
passages.original: הֶ֭אֱכַלְתָּם לֶ֣חֶם דִּמְעָ֑ה וַ֝תַּשְׁקֵ֗מוֹ בִּדְמָע֥וֹת שָׁלִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: You make us contend with our neighbors; our enemies mock us.
passages.sermon:
God of Hosts, You act with power and authority.
You make us fight with our neighbors.
Our enemies laugh at us.
You cause us to face shame from those around us.
passages.original: תְּשִׂימֵ֣נוּ מָ֭דוֹן לִשְׁכֵנֵ֑ינוּ וְ֝אֹיְבֵ֗ינוּ יִלְעֲגוּ־ לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
passages.sermon:
God of Hosts, you rule over all heavenly armies.
Restore us.
Shine your face upon us.
Save us.
passages.original: אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְבָא֣וֹת הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נוּ וְהָאֵ֥ר פָּ֝נֶ֗יךָ וְנִוָּשֵֽׁעָה׃

passages.text: You uprooted a vine from Egypt; You drove out the nations and transplanted it.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
God took a vine out of Egypt.
God removed the vine from its old place.
God drove out other nations.
God planted the vine in a new land.
passages.original: גֶּ֭פֶן מִמִּצְרַ֣יִם תַּסִּ֑יעַ תְּגָרֵ֥שׁ גּ֝וֹיִ֗ם וַתִּטָּעֶֽהָ׃

passages.text: You cleared the ground for it, and it took root and filled the land.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power and care.
God cleared the ground for the vine.
The vine took root in the ground.
The vine filled the land.
passages.original: פִּנִּ֥יתָ לְפָנֶ֑יהָ וַתַּשְׁרֵ֥שׁ שָׁ֝רָשֶׁ֗יהָ וַתְּמַלֵּא־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: The mountains were covered by its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches.
passages.sermon:
God brought Israel out of Egypt.
God planted Israel in a new land.
Israel is like a vine.
The vine grew very large.
Its shade covered the mountains.
Its branches reached the mighty cedar trees.
passages.original: כָּסּ֣וּ הָרִ֣ים צִלָּ֑הּ וַ֝עֲנָפֶ֗יהָ אַֽרְזֵי־ אֵֽל׃

passages.text: It sent out its branches to the Sea, and its shoots toward the River.
passages.sermon:
God planted a vine for His people Israel.
The vine grew strong.
Its branches reached all the way to the Sea.
Its shoots stretched out toward the River.
The vine spread far and wide.
passages.original: תְּשַׁלַּ֣ח קְצִירֶ֣הָ עַד־ יָ֑ם וְאֶל־ נָ֝הָ֗ר יֽוֹנְקוֹתֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Why have You broken down its walls, so that all who pass by pick its fruit?
passages.sermon:
God planted a vine.
God protected the vine with walls.
God broke down the walls around the vine.
Now, anyone who passes by can pick the fruit from the vine.
passages.original: לָ֭מָּה פָּרַ֣צְתָּ גְדֵרֶ֑יהָ וְ֝אָר֗וּהָ כָּל־ עֹ֥בְרֵי דָֽרֶךְ׃

passages.text: The boar from the forest ravages it, and the creatures of the field feed upon it.
passages.sermon:
A wild boar comes from the forest.
The boar destroys the vine.
Creatures from the field come.
The creatures eat the vine.
passages.original: יְכַרְסְמֶ֣נָּֽה חֲזִ֣יר מִיָּ֑עַר וְזִ֖יז שָׂדַ֣י יִרְעֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Return, O God of Hosts, we pray! Look down from heaven and see! Attend to this vine— the root Your right hand has planted, the son You have raised up for Yourself.
passages.sermon:
God of Hosts, you are mighty and powerful.
We ask you to return to us.
Look down from heaven.
See what has happened.
Pay attention to this vine.
You planted this vine with your own right hand.
You made it grow strong for yourself.
You raised up a son for yourself.
passages.original: אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְבָאוֹת֮ שֽׁ֫וּב־ נָ֥א הַבֵּ֣ט מִשָּׁמַ֣יִם וּרְאֵ֑ה וּ֝פְקֹ֗ד גֶּ֣פֶן זֹֽאת׃ וְ֭כַנָּה אֲשֶׁר־ נָטְעָ֣ה יְמִינֶ֑ךָ וְעַל־ בֵּ֝֗ן אִמַּ֥צְתָּה לָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Your vine has been cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.
passages.sermon:
God planted a vine with His own right hand.
Enemies cut down this vine.
They burned the vine with fire.
God rebuked them with His face.
They perished because of God's rebuke.
passages.original: שְׂרֻפָ֣ה בָאֵ֣שׁ כְּסוּחָ֑ה מִגַּעֲרַ֖ת פָּנֶ֣יךָ יֹאבֵֽדוּ׃

passages.text: Let Your hand be upon the man at Your right hand, on the son of man You have raised up for Yourself.
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord of Hosts.
God has great power and authority.
God, place Your hand on the man at Your right hand.
This man stands in a position of honor and favor.
Place Your hand also on the son of man.
You, God, have made this son of man strong for Yourself.
passages.original: תְּֽהִי־ יָ֭דְךָ עַל־ אִ֣ישׁ יְמִינֶ֑ךָ עַל־ בֶּן־ אָ֝דָ֗ם אִמַּ֥צְתָּ לָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Then we will not turn away from You; revive us, and we will call on Your name.
passages.sermon: We will not turn away from You.\r\nYou revive us.\r\nWe call on Your name.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ נָס֥וֹג מִמֶּ֑ךָּ תְּ֝חַיֵּ֗נוּ וּבְשִׁמְךָ֥ נִקְרָֽא׃

passages.text: Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God of Hosts.
He rules over all heavenly armies.
Restore us, LORD God of Hosts.
Shine Your face upon us.
Save us.
passages.original: יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְבָא֣וֹת הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נוּ הָאֵ֥ר פָּ֝נֶ֗יךָ וְנִוָּשֵֽׁעָה׃
